text:
Zach Werenski won the Norris Trophy last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him fourth among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement. This season has been quieter, and the context is a team in a hole: Columbus has lost five straight.

He's still playing 27:58 a night with 15 points in 18 games, 40 blocked shots and 58 shots of his own. Two goals on 3.5 expected is a little unlucky. The bigger warning runs the other way: the Blue Jackets have scored 7.3 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which is padding his assists. At five on five they're getting 48.5% of the expected goals with him out there, roughly even with how they do without him, which is not the play-driving profile he had a year ago (98th percentile among defensemen by Evolving-Hockey's measure).

What to watch: his ice time has dropped 2:02 a night over the last ten games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than almost any defenseman last season. When those chances come back, he'll look like himself again.
headline: Werenski's points are steadier than Columbus
